contents.name: Finite Automata – Computation / Strings and languages
A string is a finite sequence of symbols in Σ
A language is a set of strings
The empty string ε is the string of length 0
Regular expressions
contents.reason: The current page stops before any syntax/denotation formalism. The regular-expression grammar, denotation map, and theorems linking it to automata are all deliberately queued for `regular-expressions-and-kleenes-theorem`.

contents.name: Closure Properties for Regular Languages: closure under union
contents.reason: The lecture's closure proof is already machine-specific: it constructs a product automaton. That belongs on `deterministic-finite-automata-and-regular-languages`, not on the pre-automata vocabulary page where only the language operations themselves are being fixed.

contents.name: 〈x0, x1, …, xk〉 encodes objects as a single string
A TM has three possible outcomes for each input
contents.reason: The accept / reject / loop trichotomy first becomes precise on `turing-machines-configurations-and-computation`, where the track defines accepting and rejecting configurations, halting computations, divergence, and recognized versus decided languages. Page 581 only fixes the pre-machine encoding vocabulary.

contents.name: T-recognizable
contents.reason: Recognizability is a machine-semantic notion and is one of the opening definitions on `decidable-recognizable-and-enumerable-languages`. Page 581 has not yet defined Turing machines or machine acceptance.

contents.name: T-decidable
contents.reason: Decidability by total Turing-machine halting is postponed with the rest of the recognizability package to `decidable-recognizable-and-enumerable-languages`, where the machine model and totality distinction already exist.

contents.name: Acceptance Problem for DFAs
contents.reason: The DFA membership algorithm is one of the regular-language decision procedures that the later regular-expression page explicitly plans to package together with emptiness, finiteness, equivalence, and containment.

contents.name: Acceptance Problem for NFAs
contents.reason: This result depends on the subset construction and the regular-language decision bundle. Those appear only after the DFA and NFA pages, so the present vocabulary page records it but does not build it.

contents.name: Emptiness Problem for DFAs
contents.reason: The graph-search emptiness test is part of the later regular-language decision-problem package. It uses the automaton structure that page 581 has not yet introduced.

contents.name: Equivalence problem for DFAs
contents.reason: The equivalence algorithm relies on symmetric difference and emptiness for regular languages. The track reserves that combined decidability theorem for `regular-expressions-and-kleenes-theorem`.

contents.name: Acceptance Problem for CFGs
contents.reason: CFG membership is planned only after Chomsky normal form and the parsing machinery are in place. Those ingredients live on `context-free-pumping-ogden-and-parsing`, not on the current definitions page.

contents.name: Emptiness Problem for CFGs
contents.reason: The variable-marking emptiness argument is part of the later context-free decision package. It is not a prerequisite for the language and encoding conventions fixed on page 581.

contents.name: Equivalence Problem for CFGs
contents.reason: The track handles CFG equivalence where the undecidable language and grammar problems are gathered, alongside PCP and CFG universality and ambiguity. Recording it earlier would separate it from the reduction machinery it actually needs.

contents.name: Acceptance Problem for TMs
contents.reason: Machine acceptance is the opening definitional object of the halting-problem page. Page 581 only prepares the encoding language that later lets that semantic problem be stated cleanly.
